subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should maintainers accept the open PR's scoped ENOENT fallback in the read tool for bare daily-memory filenames, or require the fix to move upstream to the context path that loses the prefix?
rationale: Both choices fix the reported bug, but the fallback changes read-tool behavior for missing bare `YYYY-MM-DD.md` paths and touches the workspace sandbox boundary, which needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Accept scoped fallback
options.body: Land the open PR if maintainers accept that bare date reads can fall back to canonical daily memory after a root-level ENOENT while preserving the sandbox guard.

options.title: Move fix upstream
options.body: Ask the PR to preserve or repair the `memory/` prefix before the tool call if maintainers do not want read-tool date inference.

options.title: Close candidate PR and keep issue
options.body: Reject the current fix shape but keep this issue open as the canonical bug until a different implementation exists.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped fallback
recommendation.body: Land the open PR if maintainers accept that bare date reads can fall back to canonical daily memory after a root-level ENOENT while preserving the sandbox guard.

likelyOwner.reason: Startup-context ownership makes this the best available owner for deciding whether the fix belongs upstream or at the read-tool boundary.
